summary: Desktop: a message sent while its chat is still opening, switching provider instance ("Switching to <profile>...") or starting its agent is no longer refused with a red "Your draft is held. Send when ready." error. It is accepted at once and shown as a queued row (the existing Queued bar, with "sends when the chat is ready" and Cancel; no Send now). When the wait ends the held messages are sent in order, each once and with queue delivery, so none steers into the turn before it; a message held while they go out joins the end. When the open resolves to the chat's live root id, the held messages move with it. Images and pills go through the same send call. When the switch or open fails, the messages go back to the composer (text as the agent would read it, pills expanded, images kept) and the failure shows in the wait banner then, also when no pane shows the chat. A declined "Start fresh" during a switch also returns them. A send the chat refuses after the wait goes back to the composer with the ones after it, and a system row says why. Cancel on the row, or Stop, takes the messages back. While the chat still opens, its message list is hidden behind the loading skeleton, so the held messages show as queued rows under the skeleton, with Cancel. Held messages live in a renderer service, so a pane that closes during the wait does not lose them. Phones: the Expo app (while a thread loads, starts its agent or switches provider) and native Android (while a profile switch is in flight) now do the same. The message goes into the phone's durable outbox at once and shows as a queued bubble; the outbox holds that thread's delivery until the wait ends, then sends in order, each once. A failed wait (or a declined Start fresh on the Expo app) withdraws the held messages from the outbox and puts them back in the composer with their images. Leaving the chat during the wait releases the hold, and a hold never survives an app restart.

sharedBackendApi.reason: No wire, IPC or backend change. The renderer holds the message and later sends it with the existing submit-user-turn call and queue delivery.

storageDataMigration.reason: Nothing new is stored. A held message is in renderer memory only until it is sent; a quit during the wait loses it, as a refused send's composer state was not stored either beyond the draft text.

updateRelease.reason: Ships with the next desktop build. No native module, permission, signing, package identity or update channel change.
